checks.claim: Sector-local observables have vanishing cross-blocks.
checks.note: Wick–Wightman–Wigner superselection: inaccessible sectors force ⊕, not a coherent sum.

checks.claim: Three 2D sectors add to dimension 6, they do not multiply to 8.
checks.note: Alternatives add dimensions. Subsystems would multiply them.

checks.claim: Branch weights form a probability vector.
checks.note: Admissible state is ⊕ p_a rho_a, not a coherent superposition.

checks.claim: Each block trace equals its sector weight.
checks.note: Block trace is the sector probability.

checks.claim: Which-sector inaccessibility sets interference visibility to zero.
checks.note: A coherent sum would be a different physical claim.

checks.claim: Environment-induced selection leaves a diagonal ensemble in the pointer basis.
checks.note: Quantum Darwinism supplies the selection story; the ensemble is still a mixture.

checks.claim: Exclusive branches cannot be a joint sample of coexisting factors.
checks.note: Probability of a union adds. Probability of a joint factors only for coexisting variables.

checks.claim: Block-diagonal algebra is smaller than the full matrix algebra.
checks.note: dim ⊕ M_2 = 12; dim M_6 = 36. Cross-observables are the missing 24.

checks.claim: A Kraus map that is block diagonal cannot create cross-sector coherence.
checks.note: Stinespring dilation of a sector-local channel stays in the direct sum.

checks.claim: Sector probabilities are ordinary multinomial frequencies.
checks.note: Estimation does not require a tensor Hilbert space.

checks.claim: Unresolved sector entropy is the Shannon entropy of p.
checks.note: Suffering is not identified with this entropy; the statistic only measures unresolved selection.

checks.claim: Failure of branch selection is total variation from a one-hot weight.
checks.note: Psychotic-analogue regime in this formal model is tv > 0, not a tensor entanglement.

checks.claim: Embedded sectors are orthogonal as subspaces even if blocks are full rank inside.
checks.note: Orthogonality is in the direct-sum embedding, not inside a block.

checks.family: Spectral radius of a block generator
checks.claim: Spectral radius of a direct sum is the max of the block radii.
checks.note: A single ρ > 1 claim must name the time base. Here the discrete radius is the max block radius.

checks.claim: Every block radius below 1 implies the direct-sum map is asymptotically stable.
checks.note: This does not license a universal clinical threshold at 0.95.

checks.claim: A perfect blanket drives I(internal; external | blanket) below the raw mutual information.
checks.note: Markov blanket: internal ⊥ external | blanket. Active-inference measurement model.

checks.claim: Without the blanket conditioner, internal and external still share information.
checks.note: High raw mutual information is coupling, not insulation. This is the sign error in CI_B = I/H.

checks.claim: Coexisting inputs require a joint, hence a tensor of variable spaces, before atoms are defined.
checks.note: Williams–Beer atoms are defined on a joint distribution, not on a direct sum of alternatives.

checks.claim: Directed dependence is a property of a joint process.
checks.note: Schreiber transfer entropy lives on a product of time-indexed variables.

checks.claim: Partial correlation can fall once the common driver is conditioned on.
checks.note: PCMCI-style conditioning is the empirical blanket test.

checks.claim: A cut score is only defined after factors coexist in a joint.
checks.note: Used only as a partition score. Not a clinical index and not Φ as a psychosis measure.

checks.claim: A product state has Schmidt rank 1 across the cut.
checks.note: np.kron is the tensor product of coexisting factors.

checks.claim: Blanket failure as entanglement is a tensor-product predicate.
checks.note: Direct-sum sectors cannot be entangled with each other; they are alternatives.

checks.claim: Two nonzero Schmidt coefficients mark a non-product joint.
checks.note: This predicate is unavailable in a direct-sum sector model.

checks.claim: A screen is a cut of a joint system, so the ambient space is a tensor product.
checks.note: Even a bulk-boundary split is ⊗. It does not by itself force a psychosis sector sum.

checks.claim: A channel on one factor is I ⊗ E, which is defined only in a tensor product.
checks.note: Sector noise would instead be ⊕ E_a.

checks.claim: Seven coordinate axes span a 7D tangent space.
checks.note: Configuration space is a product of intervals.

checks.claim: Tensoring seven lines yields a 1D space.
checks.note: This is why the seven-tuple must not be written with ⊗.

checks.claim: The tangent space of a product is the direct sum of the factor tangents.
checks.note: This ⊕ is forced by the product manifold, not by branch inaccessibility.

checks.claim: Seven differently unitized coordinates are a tuple, not a vector in one Hilbert space.
checks.note: A master functional that multiplies them is dimensionally inhomogeneous.

checks.claim: The pocket state (P, B, T) is a coordinate projection, not a partial trace.
checks.note: Partial trace is the tensor operation. Projection is the Cartesian operation.

checks.claim: Severity on a product space needs an explicit metric; Euclidean distance is a choice.
checks.note: Replaces an unnormalized seven-dimensional polytope radius.

checks.family: Proper scoring of a scalar index
checks.claim: A collapse probability must be a calibrated map, not an algebraic combination of raw coordinates.
checks.note: PSI as written is not a probability when sigma exceeds its critical value.

checks.claim: Lag-1 autocorrelation of one coordinate can rise without a sector sum.
checks.note: Early-warning literature on prodromal symptom series. tau must be defined by the sampling rate.

checks.claim: Sample excess-related kurtosis of a Gaussian sits near 3, not at a universal cut of 8.
checks.note: Heavy tails need a model comparison, not a fixed kurtosis threshold.

checks.claim: A heavier-tailed model can outscore a Gaussian on the same coordinate.
checks.note: WAIC or ELPD should choose the noise family. A 4.8 percent cut is not derived.

checks.claim: A recovery threshold below the collapse threshold is a separate parameter.
checks.note: The gap must be estimated from trajectories. The values here are illustrative only.

checks.claim: A coordinate can jump without any of the other six moving.
checks.note: Supports a product space: coordinates are not factors of one entangled vector.

checks.claim: A recoverable coordinate has a posterior rank near one half under the prior predictive.
checks.note: Parameters should be recoverable in simulation before any subject is scored.

checks.claim: Control cost is computed on an identified dynamical matrix, not on a symbolic rho.
checks.note: Gu et al. network control is a method family. It does not set a clinical cascade order by itself.

checks.claim: Precision is an inverse variance on one error channel.
checks.note: Aberrant salience can be a high precision on noise. It is not a log-ratio capped at +2.

checks.claim: A sensory residual is a difference on one channel, not a new sector.
checks.note: Inner-speech and corollary-discharge models remain competing explanations of voices.

checks.claim: Learning-rate coordinates can be stacked without tensoring the axes.
checks.note: Mathys-style hierarchical Gaussian filtering. Stacking is a product, not a tensor of lines.

checks.claim: Clinical items stay on an ordinal layer above the coordinates.
checks.note: Coordinates do not replace validated scales.

checks.claim: Equal state deviation need not imply equal disorder once distress is a multiplier.
checks.note: Matches the pocket rule: disorder is deviation times distress, impairment, and duration.

checks.claim: A social covariate can be another axis. It is not a second reality sector unless inaccessibility is claimed.
checks.note: Contagion models should be fit on networks before any CI_B network claim.

checks.claim: An agent monitor can be expected calibration error on its own axis.
checks.note: Reward hacking is not identified with spectral radius above 1.

checks.claim: Branches use ⊕, blanket factors use ⊗, coordinates use a Cartesian product.
checks.note: The master-equation product of branch vectors remains undefined and is not generated.
